recommendations.name: Sushi Sho
recommendations.reason: Kaiten Sushi Ginza Onodera got a 5 for freshness, friendliness and a nice room - Sushi Sho is the same Edomae lineage taken further: a tiny counter omakase where the chef hands each piece over personally, which is exactly the food-5/service-5 combination that Onodera earned from you.
recommendations.avoids: The opposite of Restaurant 604's quiet-1 problem - it is a reservation-only counter of about a dozen seats where conversation stays low, and unlike Katsumidori the room is new and polished, not outdated.
recommendations.dish: The omakase progression, especially the kohada and the anago at the end
recommendations.diet_fit: Pescatarian-perfect: the entire omakase is fish, shellfish, tamago and rice, with no meat courses at all.

recommendations.name: Sasabune
recommendations.reason: You rated two sushi bars highly but noted the limits of each - Katsumidori's dated interior, Onodera's conveyor format. Sasabune is the chef's-choice 'trust me' room that keeps Onodera's fish quality without a belt or a tablet between you and the sushi.
recommendations.avoids: Steers clear of the tablet-and-conveyor bustle of Katsumidori Sushi Tokyo and the noise that sank Monkeypod Kitchen; the dining room is deliberately hushed.
recommendations.dish: Warm-rice omakase - the halibut with ponzu and the blue crab hand roll
recommendations.diet_fit: Omakase is fish and shellfish throughout; nothing meat-based on the sushi menu.

recommendations.name: Yohei Sushi
recommendations.reason: A quiet neighborhood Edomae counter in Kapalama that locals use for the same reason you go back to Kaiten Sushi Ginza Onodera - consistently fresh fish and genuinely warm service, which matches your 5.0 service average.
recommendations.avoids: No loud bar scene of the kind that dropped Monkeypod Kitchen to a 3; it is a calm, small dining room rather than a music-driven one.
recommendations.diet_fit: Sushi, sashimi and chirashi make up the core of the menu - a pescatarian can eat the whole list.

recommendations.name: Mina’s Fish House
recommendations.reason: You said Roy's Ko Olina had food-5 presentation but a vibe-2 dated interior. Mina's is the same high-end Ko Olina price bracket with the room fixed: open, airy Four Seasons dining overlooking the lagoon, and whole-fish cookery in Roy's league.
recommendations.avoids: Directly fixes what you flagged at Roy's Ko Olina - the tired interior - and it is a spacious resort room, not a music-over-conversation space like Monkeypod Kitchen a few minutes away.
recommendations.dish: Whole fish for the table, chosen off the daily catch board
recommendations.diet_fit: Built around fish: whole moi or onaga, ahi crudo, lobster pot pie, shellfish tower - the pescatarian has the best of the menu.

recommendations.name: ‘AMA‘AMA – Contemporary Island Cooking
recommendations.reason: The Kini Room scored 5 on vibe and value largely for terrace seating and atmosphere; 'AMA'AMA gives you the same open-air oceanfront setting minutes from home, with contemporary island cooking closer to Roy's food quality than to a bar menu.
recommendations.avoids: Open-air and ocean-facing rather than amplified - no loud interior music of the sort that pulled Monkeypod Kitchen down to quiet-1.
recommendations.diet_fit: Fish-forward menu: catch of the day, seared ahi and shellfish appetizers; the kitchen is used to plating the fish preparations without meat garnishes.

recommendations.name: MW Restaurant
recommendations.reason: This is the local answer to what you liked at Rigo Spanish Italian - refined cooking, careful plating and a room that feels like an occasion. Chef-driven modern Hawaii cuisine, and like Roy's it delivers on dessert, which you singled out.
recommendations.avoids: A calm, softly-lit dining room with spaced tables - the opposite of Restaurant 604, where you scored quiet 1 and said the food was only ok.
recommendations.dish: Mochi-crusted local fish; save room for the candy bar dessert
recommendations.diet_fit: Fresh island fish entrees (opakapaka, onaga) and vegetable-based starters; ask for the mochi-crusted fish preparation rather than the meat plates.

recommendations.name: Mud Hen Water
recommendations.reason: Small-plates format with real cooking behind it - the same 'good food plus a room you want to sit in' balance you praised at The Kini Room and Rigo, but with island ingredients instead of Mediterranean ones. Strong mocktail and non-alcoholic drink program too, which you've called out twice.
recommendations.avoids: A low-key Kaimuki dining room rather than a music venue; nothing like the too-loud music you docked Monkeypod Kitchen for.
recommendations.diet_fit: Poke, whole fried fish, limu and vegetable small plates, and taro/vegetable dishes make a full pescatarian meal.

recommendations.name: Bernini
recommendations.reason: Rigo Spanish Italian was a 5 on both food and vibe; Bernini is the closest thing on the island to that Italian-with-a-Japanese-technique idea, an intimate Honolulu dining room doing pasta with local seafood.
recommendations.avoids: Small and quiet by design - not the noise level that made you rate Restaurant 604 a 3 despite decent food.
recommendations.diet_fit: Seafood pastas (uni, crab, shrimp), carpaccio-style fish starters and vegetable primi give a pescatarian a full three courses.

recommendations.name: Giovedi
recommendations.reason: cino got a 4 from you for authentic Italian but only a 3 on vibe for the dark interior. Giovedi is the same handmade-pasta idea in a brighter, more personal room - the food thread from cino and Rigo without the cave feeling.
recommendations.avoids: Avoids cino's dim, closed-in interior, and it is a small quiet restaurant rather than a loud one like Monkeypod Kitchen.
recommendations.diet_fit: Handmade pastas with seafood or tomato/vegetable sauces, plus seafood antipasti; confirm the daily specials, as some are meat-based.

recommendations.name: Paesano
recommendations.reason: A long-standing family-run Italian that hits the value axis you scored 5 at Onkee Korean Grill House while carrying the same red-sauce authenticity you liked at cino - generous portions, no scene, food first.
recommendations.avoids: Quiet suburban Mililani dining room - nothing like the noise complaints you logged at Restaurant 604 and Monkeypod Kitchen.
recommendations.diet_fit: Eggplant parmigiana, linguine with clams, shrimp scampi and marinara pastas are all standard here for the pescatarian.

recommendations.name: Mimi's Peruvian Cuisine
recommendations.reason: A genuinely new direction for your list: Peruvian ceviche is raw-fish craft in the same family as the sushi you rate 5s, but with lime, chili and herbs instead of rice. Small family kitchen with the kind of attentive service you gave Onkee a 5 for.
recommendations.avoids: A tiny, low-volume room - no amplified music of the kind that capped Monkeypod Kitchen at 3.
recommendations.dish: Ceviche mixto with sweet potato and choclo
recommendations.diet_fit: Ceviche, jalea (fried seafood), arroz con mariscos and chaufa de mariscos are all pescatarian mains; skip the lomo saltado section.

recommendations.name: Middle Eats
recommendations.reason: You reward places where the food punches above the room (Onkee, food 5 / value 5). This is a small, fresh Middle Eastern kitchen doing mezze and grills - a cuisine nowhere on your list yet, and one built for sharing plates the way you enjoyed at The Kini Room.
recommendations.avoids: Counter-service calm rather than a bar with live music; avoids the loudness that sank Restaurant 604 for you.
recommendations.diet_fit: Falafel plates, hummus and mutabbal with pita, fattoush and rice-and-vegetable platters make a substantial meat-free meal; some locations also do a grilled fish plate.

recommendations.name: Tadka Indian Cuisine
recommendations.reason: Nothing Indian in your library yet, and it is the cuisine that best rewards the value-plus-flavor combination you praised at Onkee Korean Grill House - lunch thalis and curries that overdeliver for the price.
recommendations.avoids: A quiet strip-mall dining room, the opposite of the loud-music problem you flagged at Monkeypod Kitchen.
recommendations.diet_fit: Extensive vegetarian half of the menu - paneer tikka masala, chana masala, dal, baingan bharta with naan - plus fish or shrimp curry options.

recommendations.name: Water Drop Vegetarian House
recommendations.reason: Your Chinese entry is missing entirely, and this solves the pescatarian question outright: a fully vegetarian Chinese kitchen where the whole menu is in play rather than one safe dish. Cheap and generous in the way that earned Onkee its value 5.
recommendations.avoids: Calm, no-scene dining room - none of the volume that made Restaurant 604 a 3 for you.
recommendations.diet_fit: Entirely vegetarian: mock-meat clay pots, braised tofu, vegetable noodle soups and stir-fried greens - every main is safe for the pescatarian and the rest of the table eats well too.

recommendations.name: Kahumana - Organic Farm & Café
recommendations.reason: The Kini Room got a 5 on vibe for terrace seating and setting; Kahumana is the daytime version of that - open-air tables looking out over the farm in Waianae, with produce picked yards away. Quiet in a way nothing else on your list is.
recommendations.avoids: About as far from Monkeypod Kitchen's loud music as Oahu offers - the soundtrack is birds and wind, not a PA.
recommendations.diet_fit: Largely vegetarian and vegan menu - farm curry, veggie burgers, big garden salads with grains - plus a regular fish special; the pescatarian has the run of it.

recommendations.name: Olay's Thai Lao Cuisine
recommendations.reason: You've got no Thai or Lao on the list at all, and what the Onkee entry suggests you enjoy - big-flavor, well-priced, unfussy cooking with real heat - is exactly this kitchen's territory. Lao dishes give it an edge over generic Thai.
recommendations.avoids: Small neighborhood room, no live music - avoids the noise issue you scored 1 on at both Monkeypod Kitchen and Restaurant 604.
recommendations.diet_fit: Papaya salad, tofu or shrimp pad kee mao, green curry with tofu, and whole fried fish with chili-lime; ask for no meat in the larb and request vegetarian versions where needed.

recommendations.name: TsuruTonTan
recommendations.reason: Your Japanese ratings are all sushi - this is the other side of it, hand-cut udon in enormous bowls, and it lands the same food-quality-first appeal as Katsumidori without the dated interior you docked it for.
recommendations.avoids: Unlike Katsumidori Sushi Tokyo's outdated room, this is a modern, well-designed space; the dining room is conversational rather than the blasting-music environment of Monkeypod Kitchen.
recommendations.diet_fit: Mentaiko cream udon, tempura shrimp udon, and cold udon with grated yam are pescatarian mains; ask for the katsuo-based broth rather than any pork additions.

recommendations.name: Maguro Spot
recommendations.reason: A lower-key counterpart to the sushi you rate highly - the same emphasis on fresh ahi that won Kaiten Sushi Ginza Onodera its food 5, at a price point that matches the value you liked in Onkee's lunch specials.
recommendations.avoids: Tiny, quiet counter with no music program at all - nothing like Monkeypod Kitchen's volume.
recommendations.dish: Spicy ahi and shoyu ahi combo bowl
recommendations.diet_fit: Poke bowls are all fish - ahi, salmon, tako - over rice or salad; entirely pescatarian-safe.

recommendations.name: Haleʻiwa Beach House
recommendations.reason: The Kini Room's 5 was about terrace seating, mocktails and a beautiful room; this is the North Shore equivalent - open-sided dining with an ocean view and fish-centered cooking, worth the drive as a destination meal rather than a nearby default.
recommendations.avoids: Open-air and breezy rather than an enclosed room with speakers - steers well clear of the loud-music mark that held Monkeypod Kitchen to a 3.
recommendations.diet_fit: Fresh catch, seared ahi, fish tacos, poke and a grain/vegetable bowl - a full pescatarian dinner without adaptation.

recommendations.name: Appetito Craft Pizza & Wine Bar
recommendations.reason: You gave Moku Kitchen a 4 mostly for the pizza and liked cino's authentic Italian; Appetito is the sit-down version of both - blistered crusts and proper pastas in a calm wine-bar room rather than a warehouse.
recommendations.avoids: A small, seated wine-bar space, not the cavernous loud hall that made Restaurant 604 a quiet-1 for you.
recommendations.dish: Margherita pizza with the burrata starter
recommendations.diet_fit: Margherita and marinara pizzas, spaghetti alle vongole, seafood risotto and caprese give the pescatarian a full meal.
